extracted.intended_audience: scholars and researchers preparing manuscript submissions to the American Political Science Review (APSR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting manuscripts to the American Political Science Review, including scope/quality expectations, track definitions, formatting/length, anonymization, reproducibility, ethics, and transfer policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and Aims — scholarly quality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The APSR publishes scholarly research of exceptional merit: problem-driven scholarship that is well conceptualized, ethically designed, and well executed, meeting the highest ethical and scholarly standards for research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should address timely and timeless questions about power and governance central to the study of politics everywhere; represent diversity of subfields, geographic areas, identities, methods, and approaches; be original, innovative, and well-crafted; and employ the methodologies and methods most appropriate to the problems they address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track suitability — Regular Articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular Articles that use original work to advance understanding of important issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit to the Regular Articles track when presenting full, original empirical or theoretical contributions that advance the literature on important issues in political science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track suitability — Research Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Notes are intended for shorter, more focused articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Research Notes track for concise pieces that address a specific question or present a focused result that does not require a full-length article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track suitability — Replications and Reappraisals
rubrics_metrics.description: Replications and Reappraisals revisit results previously published in the APSR or in other journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit replication studies or reappraisals that rigorously reexamine prior findings; follow reproducibility and transparency expectations described elsewhere in the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track suitability — Syntheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntheses summarize a field of research and usually include some empirical analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow further instructions for the Synthesis track available on the APSR site; the piece should provide an integrative overview and typically include empirical work to support synthesis claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track suitability — Registered Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered Reports are submitted prior to any data analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this track for studies where the research plan (hypotheses, design, analysis plan) is peer-reviewed before data collection/analysis; follow the registered reports procedures described by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and word count requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no strict word limit for the APSR, but most articles are expected to be less than 11,000 words; research notes should be less than 7,000 words. Wordcounts exclude appendices and reference lists. Abstracts must be 150 words or less. All manuscripts should include a word count on the front page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided word count tool for PDFs; follow specific length guidance for special tracks (e.g., syntheses) and ensure abstract ≤150 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and preservation of blind review
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be written in such a way that they preserve the anonymity of the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid citing yourself unnecessarily or excessively and ensure that any self-citation does not reveal identity; remove obvious references to the author (e.g., “As I wrote in 1993,…”) to ensure anonymous review.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID identifier requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning January 1, 2019, an ORCID iD is a requirement for corresponding authors submitting to APSR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Editorial Manager system will prompt authors to attach an ORCID iD during submission; authors may update their Editorial Manager profile in advance. Including an ORCID improves discoverability and supports automatic updates to your publication record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication and originality policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The APSR publishes only original work. Authors with work under review or published that is similar or closely related to their submitted manuscript must notify the editors in their cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Cambridge’s Preprint Policy for exceptions; disclose related submissions or publications up front so editors can assess overlap and originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-analysis plans and pre-registration expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: APSR encourages preregistration of empirical research questions and main analyses and generally expects preregistration for experiments and any study testing hypotheses on prospective data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your study references a pre-analysis plan or pre-registration, APSR expects you to: Share — include an anonymized version of the registration/pre-analysis plan in your online appendix or link to an anonymized version (e.g., via OSF). Signpost — clearly mark which analyses are registered and which are unregistered/exploratory. Evaluate — indicate in the text whether results align with preregistered expectations. Reconcile — when analyses deviate from registrations, provide a reconciliation report (a) indicating which analyses were modified or dropped, (b) justifying modifications/drops, and (c) when possible, reporting what conclusions would have been if the original analyses were implemented; place this in an appendix and indicate major deviations clearly in the manuscript text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and reproducibility standards (DA*RT)
rubrics_metrics.description: APSR will collaborate with authors to meet DA*RT standards and recognizes many ways to meet those standards depending on the type of scholarship, research context, and other factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide clear and transparent communication about procedures used to collect and analyze evidence; make work as accessible and reproducible as possible across subfields and approaches; when data cannot be shared for ethical/legal reasons, authors should contact the editors before review and explain constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility package requirement and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a conditionally accepted manuscript substantially relies on computation, authors will be required to deposit a reproducibility package containing data, code, and documentation necessary for other scholars to reproduce the manuscript’s findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal will verify that the package reproduces the paper’s results and is documented well enough for future researchers to understand and benefit; detailed guidelines for reproducibility packages are provided by the APSR and should be followed. Authors who anticipate problems adhering to guidelines for legal/ethical reasons should contact editors prior to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal theory and proofs requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers containing formal theory should be submitted with complete proofs, either in the text or as Supplementary Material, to be available to the reviewers and editors during the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal claims will be reviewed in detail by an editor and assistants at the conditional acceptance stage for consistency and readability. Authors are expected to collaborate with the journal in addressing any potential issues raised by this technical verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication scrutiny and corrections policy (COPE adherence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal follows COPE guidelines scrupulously; errors discovered after publication may entail a retraction, corrigendum, or expression of concern. The Journal publishes replications and encourages comments on each article’s DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should carefully consider reproducibility and reliability before submission and openly acknowledge weaknesses, assumptions, and limitations. The journal encourages post-publication engagement and debate that focuses on scholarly correction rather than ad hominem attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical obligations for research
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must comply with APSA’s A Guide to Professional Ethics in Political Science and Principles and Guidance for Human Subjects Research. Researchers have ethical obligations to ensure that research engaging human participants adheres to APSA principles; declare participant compensation; declare potential or perceived conflicts of interest; disclose sources of financial support; facilitate evaluation through data and analytic transparency when legally/ethically possible; and acknowledge contributions (authorship and citations) appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting, authors will be asked to affirm how their practices conform to these standards. If a submission draws on human participants, authors should answer the screening question and discuss ethical practices (consent, deception, confidentiality, harm, compensation) in text or appendix. If not compliant, provide reasoned justification and include additional explanation in an appendix if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclosures and reviewer sharing of ethical materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting authors must: indicate if the submission draws on human participants; confirm compliance with APSA human subjects guidance or justify deviations; explain how other ethical issues/conflicts of interest were addressed; declare funding agencies/organizations; indicate where data collection procedures are explained; and confirm that, if accepted, quantitative data and related code necessary to produce results will be made publicly available on the APSR Dataverse or provide a reasoned justification for inability to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information (and any appendices) will be shared with reviewers as appropriate, and reviewers will be invited to comment on the extent to which the research or researchers have adequately addressed ethical and transparency obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review transfer policy — transfer out (APSR to other journal)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a paper is rejected by the APSR with reviews, the corresponding author has the option to transfer their manuscript and reviews to another participating journal within 4 weeks of their rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author requests the managing editor initiate the transfer; APSR sends the anonymized manuscript and anonymized reviews to the new editor. If the recipient journal’s editor wants reviewer identities, they may request them. The initial request for review alerts reviewers to the possibility of transfer. Authors should consult the recipient journal’s submission guidelines prior to initiating transfer and may be asked to submit a cover letter detailing changes they would make.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review transfer policy — transfer in (from other journals to APSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: APSR will accept transfer of anonymous manuscripts and identified reviews from other journals when the other journal has a transfer-out process and manuscripts were reviewed anonymously by external reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To initiate, authors submit a normal new submission and request transfer of reviews in the note to editor and arrange for the other journal to send manuscripts and reviews to apsr@apsanet.org. The paper must have been rejected fewer than 4 weeks ago. All reviews must be sent. APSR may consult prior reviewers but is under no obligation to rely on external reviews. Decisions on transferred manuscripts are final; manuscripts submitted via transfer cannot later be resubmitted as regular submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should follow the manuscript preparation guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the APSR Style Manual for Political Science and the manuscript preparation guidelines linked on the APSR submission pages for specifics on formatting, citations, figures, tables, and supplementary materials. For further questions, contact apsr@apsanet.org.
